Control settings for OptimLib algorithms

Source: R/control.R
optimlib_control.Rd

Builds a validated list of settings for optimlib(), optimlib_sumt() and optimlib_root(). Unspecified settings take OptimLib's defaults. Algorithm-specific settings are given as named lists; only the entries you supply are changed, and unknown names are an error.

Usage

optimlib_control(
  iter_max = 2000,
  grad_err_tol = 1e-08,
  rel_sol_change_tol = 1e-14,
  rel_objfn_change_tol = 1e-08,
  print_level = 0,
  conv_failure_switch = 0,
  seed = NULL,
  bfgs = list(),
  lbfgs = list(),
  cg = list(),
  gd = list(),
  nm = list(),
  de = list(),
  pso = list(),
  sumt = list(),
  broyden = list()
)

Arguments

iter_max

Maximum number of iterations (gradient-based methods, Nelder-Mead, SUMT outer loop and root finding). Population methods use n_gen in de / pso instead.

grad_err_tol

Convergence tolerance on the gradient norm.

rel_sol_change_tol

Convergence tolerance on the relative change in the parameters.

rel_objfn_change_tol

Convergence tolerance on the relative change in the objective value.

print_level

Amount of trace output, from 0 (none) to 4.

conv_failure_switch

What to do on convergence failure: 0 returns the best guess silently, 1 returns it with a message, 2 leaves par at its starting value and prints the best guess.

seed

Seed for the random number generator used by the population methods ("de", "de_prmm", "pso", "pso_dv"). If NULL (default), a seed is drawn from R's RNG, so results are reproducible with set.seed().

bfgs, lbfgs, cg, gd, nm, de, pso, sumt, broyden

Named lists of algorithm-specific settings; see Details.

Value

A list of class optimlib_control.

Details

The algorithm-specific entries and their defaults are:

  • bfgs: wolfe_cons_1 = 1e-3, wolfe_cons_2 = 0.9 (line search).

  • lbfgs: par_M = 10 (stored correction pairs), wolfe_cons_1 = 1e-3, wolfe_cons_2 = 0.9.

  • cg: method = "pr", one of "fr" (Fletcher-Reeves), "pr" (Polak-Ribiere+), "fr_pr" (hybrid), "hs" (Hestenes-Stiefel), "dy" (Dai-Yuan), "hz" (Hager-Zhang); restart_threshold = 0.1, use_rel_sol_change_crit = FALSE, wolfe_cons_1 = 1e-3, wolfe_cons_2 = 0.1.

  • gd: method = "basic", one of "basic", "momentum", "nag", "adagrad", "rmsprop", "adadelta", "adam", "nadam"; par_step_size = 0.1, step_decay = FALSE, step_decay_periods = 10, step_decay_val = 0.5, par_momentum = 0.9, par_ada_norm_term = 1e-8, par_ada_rho = 0.9, ada_max = FALSE (AdaMax / NadaMax variants), par_adam_beta_1 = 0.9, par_adam_beta_2 = 0.999, clip_grad = FALSE, clip_max_norm = FALSE, clip_min_norm = FALSE, clip_norm_type = 2, clip_norm_bound = 5.

  • nm: adaptive_pars = TRUE, par_alpha = 1 (reflection), par_beta = 0.5 (contraction), par_gamma = 2 (expansion), par_delta = 0.5 (shrinkage).

  • de (also used by "de_prmm"): n_pop = 200, n_pop_best = 6, n_gen = 1000, mutation_method = 1 (1 rand, 2 best), check_freq = Inf, par_F = 0.8, par_CR = 0.9, and for "de_prmm" pmax = 4, max_fn_eval = 1e5, par_F_l = 0.1, par_F_u = 1, par_tau_F = 0.1, par_tau_CR = 0.1, par_d_eps = 0.5. "de_prmm" ignores n_gen: its budget is set by max_fn_eval and pmax, and it halves the population three times, so it needs n_pop %/% 8 > n_pop_best; initial_lb = NULL, initial_ub = NULL (range of the initial population; defaults to par -/+ 0.5).

  • pso (also used by "pso_dv"): center_particle = TRUE, n_pop = 200, n_gen = 1000, check_freq = Inf, inertia_method = 1 (1 linearly decreasing, 2 dampening), par_w = 1, par_w_damp = 0.99, par_w_min = 0.1, par_w_max = 0.99, velocity_method = 1 (1 fixed, 2 linear), par_c_cog = 2, par_c_soc = 2, par_final_c_cog = 0.5, par_final_c_soc = 2.5, initial_lb = NULL, initial_ub = NULL.

  • sumt: par_eta = 10 (growth factor of the penalty parameter).

  • broyden: par_rho = 0.9, par_sigma_1 = 1e-3, par_sigma_2 = 1e-3.

See the OptimLib documentation (https://optimlib.readthedocs.io/) for the meaning of each setting.

Examples

optimlib_control(iter_max = 500, lbfgs = list(par_M = 20))
#> <optimlib_control>
#>  $ iter_max            : num 500
#>  $ grad_err_tol        : num 1e-08
